rationale: The WObj body fixes the cleanup order and dereferences the cast object immediately. HSD_RObjRemoveAll's loop naturally does nothing for a null head, and HSD_AObjRemove explicitly returns for NULL, so absent attachments are handled by the callees before superclass cleanup.

evidence.why: Shows the exact RObj, AObj, and parent-release ordering and the absence of a callback-level object null check.
Shows that a NULL RObj-list head is a no-op and that non-null lists are destroyed from head to tail.
Shows that HSD_AObjRemove treats NULL as a no-op and otherwise completes subordinate cleanup before freeing the AObj.

value: For channel 4, the incoming animation scalar is clamped to `[0, 1]`, passed with `wobj->aobj->hsd_obj`'s spline to `splArcLengthPoint`, and the resulting `Vec3` is stored as the WObj position before the spline-relative flag is set. For channels 5 through 7, the scalar flows directly to the corresponding X, Y, or Z setter; those setters first convert an existing spline-relative position through the associated JObj matrix when necessary, then write the selected component and mark the position updated.
rationale: The callback directly exposes the channel-to-value flow. The position-setter implementations explain the downstream flag and coordinate-space effects of the callback's calls, while splArcLengthPoint shows that the clamped scalar is interpreted as normalized cumulative distance before curve evaluation.

evidence.why: Shows scalar clamping, spline lookup and sampling, vector assignment, relative-flag setting, and dispatch of the three direct component values.

Shows the X, Y, and Z setters converting a spline-relative stored position through the associated JObj matrix before replacing one component, clearing the relative flag, and setting the updated-position flag.
Shows splArcLengthPoint converting its scalar from normalized cumulative arc distance to a spline parameter and evaluating the resulting point.

value: Realizes animation-driven world-object path motion and positional animation: one animation channel expresses normalized distance traveled along an authored spline, producing approximately distance-uniform movement along the curve, while three other channels animate Cartesian position components directly.
rationale: The callback routes channel 4 through splArcLengthPoint after clamping it to normalized endpoints and routes channels 5 through 7 to Cartesian setters. The spline implementation confirms that the channel-4 value is converted from cumulative arc distance rather than used directly as polynomial time.

evidence.why: Shows an animation channel driving spline-point sampling and three channels driving direct Cartesian position components.
Shows normalized cumulative distance being inverted into a spline parameter before the path point is evaluated.

value: Static HSD animation-update callback with signature `void WObjUpdateFunc(void* obj, enum_t type, HSD_ObjData* val)`. The opaque object argument is interpreted as `HSD_WObj*`, `type` selects a WObj animation channel, and the handled channels consume and, for channel 4, may modify `val->fv` as a floating-point value.
rationale: The matched definition provides the exact callback signature and casts obj to HSD_WObj. Its switch reads val->fv for every supported channel, and the spline channel clamps that field in place before using it.

evidence.why: Provides the exact signature, object interpretation, channel selector, and floating-point HSD_ObjData usage.

value: Applies interpreted HSD_WObj animation channels to the object's position: channel 4 samples a point along the spline associated with the WObj's animation object, while channels 5, 6, and 7 update the X, Y, and Z position components respectively.
rationale: HSD_WObjInterpretAnim installs WObjUpdateFunc as the callback passed to HSD_AObjInterpretAnim. The callback's switch maps channel 4 to spline sampling and maps channels 5 through 7 to the three component setters, establishing its role as the WObj position-animation update routine.

evidence.why: Shows HSD_WObjInterpretAnim registering WObjUpdateFunc with the AObj interpreter and shows the callback dispatching animation channels 4 through 7 to spline or component position updates.

value: A null WObj causes no update, and unrecognized channel types are ignored. Channel 4 clamps out-of-range progress to the spline endpoints, requires a non-null AObj, associated JObj, and spline, replaces the full position, and leaves flag bit 0 set to identify the stored point as spline-relative. Channels 5 through 7 perform direct component updates; if the prior position was spline-relative, their setters convert it to the associated JObj-transformed position and clear bit 0 before changing the component.
rationale: The callback contains the null guard, channel switch, endpoint clamps, dependency assertions, and explicit flag set. The component setters show the transition from spline-relative state to transformed direct-position state.

evidence.why: Shows the null guard, ignored switch default, channel-4 clamping and assertions, full-position update, and spline-relative flag assignment.
Shows the full-vector setter clearing bit 0 and the X setter transforming and clearing an existing relative position before applying a direct component value.
Shows the equivalent spline-relative-to-direct transition in all three component setters.

value: WObj descriptors supply an initial position, reference-object description, and optionally a class name. Animation descriptions are converted into AObj and RObj attachments; interpreted animation values either select a clamped point along a JObj spline or update one position component. Position queries return the resulting Vec3, transforming spline-relative coordinates through the associated JObj matrix when required.
rationale: The current source preserves descriptor loading, animation attachment, clamped spline and per-axis updates, class-name lookup, conversion of spline-relative state through the associated JObj matrix, and final Vec3 output.

evidence.why: Shows descriptor positions and RObj descriptions being loaded, animations becoming AObj and RObj attachments, and interpreted channels selecting spline or per-axis positions.
Shows optional descriptor class lookup, direct position updates, spline-relative coordinates transformed through a JObj matrix, and resulting Vec3 queries.

value: Provides the world-position branch of HSD scene-animation playback: it attaches and requests animation controllers for world objects, evaluates authored channels that move a point along a referenced spline or directly update its X, Y, and Z coordinates, and advances associated relation-object animation.
rationale: The current animation-management and interpretation routines continue to coordinate AObj and RObj playback and map authored spline-path or per-axis channels into WObj positions.

evidence.why: Shows animation attachment and frame requests, coordinated RObj animation, and interpretation of spline-path and X, Y, and Z channels into world-object positions.

value: A C implementation unit for the class-managed HSD_WObj type. Its module state consists of an HSD_WObjInfo class descriptor and an optional HSD_ClassInfo* default-class override; its objects carry a Vec3 position, animation-object and reference-object associations, and position-state flags.
rationale: The current declarations retain the HSD_WObjInfo descriptor and nullable default-class pointer, while the methods operate on WObj animation, relation-object, position, and flag state and register the class lifecycle.

evidence.why: Declares the class descriptor and default-class pointer and shows operations on WObj AObj, RObj, position, and flags.
Shows class-aware construction and position and state-flag operations on HSD_WObj instances.
Registers HSD_WObj class metadata and installs its lifecycle methods.

value: Implements the HSD world-object subsystem: it creates and loads HSD_WObj instances, manages their animation and reference-object attachments, maintains their three-dimensional positions, and installs the class lifecycle methods used to load and release them.
rationale: The current unit still contains animation management, descriptor-driven initialization, class-aware allocation, position accessors and mutation, resource release, and lifecycle-method registration.

evidence.why: Shows WObj animation attachment, removal, requests, interpretation, and descriptor-driven position and RObj initialization.
Shows class-aware loading and allocation plus vector and per-axis position operations.
Shows AObj and RObj release and installation of WObj load, release, and amnesia methods.

value: The module permits an optional descendant class to become the default allocation class and clears that override when class amnesia reaches it. Within each WObj, animation type 4 marks the position as spline-relative with flag bit 0; direct position or axis updates clear that relative state as needed and set flag bit 1. Animation removal clears the AObj association, while release removes both AObj and RObj resources before delegating to the parent class.
rationale: Current code retains the default-class descendant guard and amnesia reset, spline-relative and direct-position flag transitions, animation removal, and release of both attachment types before parent delegation.

evidence.why: Shows animation removal clearing AObj state, type 4 selecting a clamped spline point and setting relative-position bit 0, and direct axis channels invoking position setters.
Shows descendant validation and default-class assignment plus direct vector and axis updates clearing relative state and setting bit 1.
Shows class amnesia clearing the default override and release removing RObj and AObj resources before parent delegation.
